## Why This Is Asked
This question probes integration of Identity Protection, Conditional Access, device compliance, and PIM for hardened admin access, including automation and rollback.

## Key Concepts
- Identity Protection sign-in risk and risk-based CA
- Device compliance and Hybrid Azure AD Join
- Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for Just-In-Time access
- Automated session revocation on risk events
- Sandbox validation and safe rollback

## Code Example

```powershell
# Invalidate all refresh tokens for a user to force reauth on risk event
$token = Get-GraphAccessToken -Scopes 'https://graph.microsoft.com/.default'
Invoke-RestMethod -Method POST -Uri 'https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/$userId/invalidateAllRefreshTokens' -Headers @{Authorization = 'Bearer ' + $token}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the risk policy in a sandbox without impacting production?
- What monitoring would you enable to detect abuse or misconfig and trigger fallback?

## Why This Is Asked
This evaluates your expertise in designing secure, auditable, and resilient CI/CD authentication mechanisms using certificate-based service principals rather than static secrets.

- Azure Key Vault integration for secure credential storage
- Automated certificate lifecycle management
- Rapid revocation and incident response protocols
- Pipeline runtime authentication and binding
- Comprehensive auditing and monitoring
- Disaster recovery and rollback procedures

## Code Example
```bash
# Generate and store certificate in Key Vault
az keyvault certificate create \
  --vault-name my-kv \
  --name my-sp-cert \
  --policy @certificate-policy.json

# Configure service principal with certificate
az ad sp create-for-rbac \
  --name my-ci-cd-sp \
  --cert @my-sp-cert.pem \
  --keyvault my-kv \
  --create-cert

# Pipeline runtime certificate retrieval
az keyvault secret show \
  --vault-name my-kv \
  --name my-sp-cert \
  --query value -o tsv > cert.pem
```
